svg.aria-label: Forest cross-section showing three fire types. Ground fire: smoldering in the duff and roots below the surface. Surface fire: low flames burning grass, needles, fallen branches and shrubs; tree crowns untouched. Ladder fuels: shrubs and low branches carry fire from the surface up to the crowns. Crown fire: flames in the tree tops, spreading tree-to-tree. Notes: surface fire is usually low to moderate severity, clears fuel, and big trees survive; crown fire is high severity and kills most trees.
svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Ground, surface, and crown fires
svg.text: Three types of forest fire: ground, surface, and crown
